texts.li: "Is there room for one more?" {X_nameDef} asked it at supper, to the whole table, but it was {A_nameDef} {X_pronoun} was looking at. The two of them have hardly been apart since the {FACTION} party arrived three days ago.\n\n{FACTION} won't part with one of its people for nothing. {A_nameDef} is studying the floor and trying hard not to look as if the answer matters.

Every evening since the {FACTION} people made camp by the colony, {X_nameDef} and {A_nameDef} have ended up at the same fire and stayed long after it burned down. Now {X_nameDef} wants to stay when the rest of them move on.\n\nWhoever speaks for the group has made it clear that {X_nameDef} owes them, and that they will remember who kept {X_objective}. {A_nameDef} hasn't asked the council for anything, but it's plain what {A_pronoun} wants.

The {FACTION} visitors leave at first light, and {X_nameDef} would rather not go with them. In two days {X_nameDef} has mended {A_nameDef}'s boots and learned most of the animals by name. Nothing back home is worth the walk, {X_nameDef} says.\n\n{A_nameDef} says the colony could use another pair of hands. It's clear that isn't the only reason.

li.label: Welcome {X_nameDef} in
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} unpacked in the colony that night. The rest of the {FACTION} party left at dawn without a word to anyone, and {FACTION} will remember it.

li.label: Pay {FACTION} to let {X_objective} go
li.outcome: Two hundred silver went to {FACTION} for the trouble, and {X_nameDef} stayed. One or two people have been working out what else that silver would have bought.

li.label: {X_nameDef} leaves with {X_possessive} people
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} left with {FACTION} at first light. {A_nameDef} found a fence to fix on the far side of the colony and stayed there all morning.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} walked {X_nameDef} and the {FACTION} party a good way down the road at first light. When they parted, {A_nameDef} kept walking, alone, and not toward anything in particular.

li.label: Ask our best talker to square it with {FACTION}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} sat down with whoever speaks for {FACTION} and talked until a debt had been forgiven and a promise made. {X_nameDef} stayed, and {FACTION} left on decent terms.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {B_nameDef} shared a pipe with the {FACTION} elders and talked until the fire burned low. {X_nameDef} stayed, and the elders left without hard feelings.
[b:past:trader] {B_nameDef} haggled with {FACTION} as if {X_nameDef} were a bolt of cloth, which seemed to be what they understood. {X_nameDef} stayed, and they parted on decent terms.

li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} talked with the {FACTION} visitors until dark and got nowhere. {X_nameDef} stayed anyway, and {FACTION} left angry.

texts.li: "Back home we feed that to the pigs," said {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} at dinner, looking at {A_nameDef}'s plate. Then {X_nameDef} looked at {A_nameDef} and said what they do back home with people like {A_nameDef}. Only the other visitors laughed.\n\n{A_nameDef} put down {A_possessive} spoon very slowly.

{X_nameDef} has spent the whole visit telling anyone who'll listen what is wrong with {A_nameDef}, starting with the voice and working down to the family. {A_nameDef} has heard all of it. {X_nameDef} made sure of that.\n\nThe colony would like to stay on good terms with {FACTION}. {A_nameDef} would like to know whether a guest is allowed to say anything at all.

{X_nameDef} spat on the floor {A_nameDef} swept that morning and called {A_objective} something that made the cook drop a ladle. When {A_nameDef} asked {X_nameDef} to repeat it, {X_nameDef} did, slower.\n\nGuests are safe under this roof; that has always been the rule. The way {A_nameDef} sees it, the rule ought to work both ways.

li.label: Demand an apology
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} apologized to {A_nameDef} the next morning, every word of it addressed to {X_possessive} boots.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} was told to apologize and laughed in {A_nameDef}'s face. A minute later the two of them were rolling in the dirt, and {FACTION} will hear about that too.

li.label: Let it go, they're guests
li.outcome: The council said nothing to {X_nameDef}, who took that as encouragement. {A_nameDef} ate the rest of {A_possessive} meals somewhere else until the visitors left.

li.label: Throw the lot of them out
li.outcome: The whole {FACTION} party was told to leave and walked to the gate, {X_nameDef} talking the entire way. {A_nameDef} watched them go with {A_possessive} arms folded.

li.label: Ask our best talker to settle it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} had a word with whoever leads the {FACTION} visitors. {X_nameDef} kept to the guests' side of the yard for the rest of the stay.

outcomes.li: [theirLowtech] {B_nameDef} went to the {FACTION} elders with a jug of something strong. By evening {X_nameDef} had been told off by {X_possessive} own people, and {A_nameDef} got a gruff nod across the yard.
[b:office:Speaker] The colony's speaker took the {FACTION} visitors aside and chose every word with care. {X_nameDef} said nothing more to {A_nameDef} for the rest of the stay.

li.riskOutcome: The {FACTION} visitors heard {B_nameDef} out and took {X_nameDef}'s side. {X_nameDef} has been grinning at {A_nameDef} across the yard ever since.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, has had {A_nameDef}'s heirloom in {X_possessive} hands for some time now, turning it to the light. "Good old work," {X_nameDef} says. "Collectors pay for this." It belonged to somebody now buried out back.\n\nThe offer is real silver, more than the thing is worth to anyone who didn't know its owner. {A_nameDef} hasn't said yes or no, and keeps glancing at the council.

Four offers so far, each better than the last. {X_nameDef} noticed the heirloom {A_nameDef} carries within a minute of arriving and keeps coming back to it.\n\nIt's one of the few things {A_nameDef} has left of the dead, and {A_nameDef} has left it to the council.

li.label: Sell it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} handed it over and counted the {COUNT} silver twice, then went and sat by the graves until supper.

li.label: Haggle until it hurts
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} haggled until {X_nameDef} was sweating, and got {COUNT} silver for it. {A_nameDef} watched it go into the trader's pack and didn't say another word all day.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} pushed the price once too often. {X_nameDef} put the heirloom down, said something unkind about frontier manners, and walked off. {A_nameDef} still has it, and is more relieved than {A_pronoun} expected to be.

li.label: It stays with {A_nameDef}
li.outcome: The heirloom stays with {A_nameDef}. {X_nameDef} shrugged, said everyone has a price, and seemed to think better of {A_nameDef} for refusing.

texts.li: Every night, through the cell door, {X_nameDef} tells {A_nameDef} about a field back with {FACTION} that won't plant itself, and about how none of this was ever {X_possessive} idea. {A_nameDef} believes every word.\n\nNow {A_nameDef} is asking the council to let {X_nameDef} go home. The ones who caught {X_nameDef} remember things differently.

{A_nameDef} carried {X_nameDef}'s meal down this morning and came back without the bowl and with a request. {X_nameDef} has a child back with {FACTION}, or says so, and begged {A_nameDef} to ask the council for {X_possessive} freedom.\n\nIt might be true. Prisoners say a great many things, and {A_nameDef} has never been good at telling the true ones from the rest.

li.label: Let {X_objective} go home
li.outcome: The wardens have orders to let {X_nameDef} go. {X_nameDef} thanked {A_nameDef} with both hands and swore that {FACTION} would hear how {X_pronoun} was treated here.

li.label: Hear {X_objective} out properly
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat by the cell door until late and listened to all of it. {X_nameDef} has stopped glaring at the wardens, and {A_nameDef} has started saving {X_objective} the better bread.

li.label: Keep the door locked
li.outcome: The door stays locked. {A_nameDef} still carries {X_nameDef}'s meals down, and doesn't stay to talk anymore.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} is still alive, a few steps from {A_nameDef}, both hands pressed to a wound that won't stop bleeding. A few minutes ago {X_nameDef} was trying to kill {A_objective}. Now {X_nameDef} is asking {A_objective} for help, in a voice that keeps cracking.\n\n{X_nameDef} doesn't have long.

{A_nameDef} was walking among the fallen when a hand closed on {A_possessive} ankle. It was {X_nameDef} of {FACTION}, alive and bleeding badly, begging for someone to decide what happens to {X_objective}.\n\nThe choices are a prison bed, a quick blade, or leaving {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} lies. {X_nameDef} is losing blood the whole time the council thinks about it.

li.label: Take {X_objective} prisoner
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} went to carry {X_nameDef} to a prison bed, muttering that somebody had better have made one.

li.label: End it quickly
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} knelt beside {X_nameDef}, said something too low for anyone else to hear, and made it quick.

li.label: Leave {X_objective} where {X_pronoun} lies
li.outcome: No one went back for {X_nameDef}. Toward evening the calling stopped.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} caught {A_nameDef} away from the others and asked in a low voice whether the colony could spare any food. The damp got into their stores this season. Their children have been living on bark soup, and the walk home is long.\n\n{X_nameDef} didn't beg, only stood there afterward, waiting for an answer.

{A_nameDef} counted a handful of {FACTION} people at the gate, thin as fence rails, one of them carrying a child too tired to cry. {X_nameDef} speaks for them. They want food, whatever the colony can spare.\n\nThe colony can spare some. The cooks want to know whether it can still spare it come midwinter.

li.label: Fill their sacks
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} tied the last sack shut, said thank you twice, and the {FACTION} people set off before dark, bent under the sacks. The cooks are already working out what to stretch.

li.label: Give them silver instead
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} got sixty silver and directions to the nearest market. It's a long way on empty stomachs.

li.label: Turn them away
li.outcome: The colony's food stayed in the colony's storeroom. The {FACTION} people waited until dusk, then walked on, slower than they came.

li.label: Send them home with seed, and a grower's advice
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon with {X_nameDef} going over what grows where and when, and sent {X_objective} home with a sack of food and a pouch of seed. {FACTION} should eat better next year.

outcomes.li: [winter] {B_nameDef} sent {X_nameDef} home with enough food to get through the cold and a pouch of seed for the thaw, and drew {X_objective} a map of where to plant it.

[b:past:farmer] {B_nameDef} grew up on a farm and talked {X_nameDef} through it the way {B_possessive} own parents would have, starting with the soil and ending with the weather. {FACTION} went home with seed and a sack of food.

texts.li:
"I was only reaching past it," says {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, holding up a bleeding hand.

"You were reaching into {PET_possessive} mouth," says {A_nameDef}, whose animal {PET_nameDef} is.

{FACTION} would like compensation. {A_nameDef} would like the council to remember whose side it's on.

{X_nameDef} has shown the teeth marks in {X_possessive} hand to anyone who will look. They're from {PET_definite}, {A_nameDef}'s animal, and {A_nameDef} says anyone who pats a sleeping animal on the head gets what's coming.\n\nThe {FACTION} visitors want silver for the bite. One or two of them want {PET_definite} as well.

li.label: Pay for the bite
li.outcome: The council paid {X_nameDef} eighty silver for the bite. {X_nameDef} counted it with the bandaged hand, which no longer seemed to hurt.

li.label: Stand by {PET_definite}
li.outcome: Guests keep their hands off other people's animals, and that was the end of it. {FACTION} took that badly, and {A_nameDef} gave {PET_definite} an extra helping at dinner.

li.label: Hand {PET_definite} over to them
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took {PET_definite} on a length of rope, keeping the bitten hand well out of reach. {A_nameDef} left the council table before the matter was closed.

texts.li: What was left of last night's kill is lying in the brush not far from the colony. {A_nameDef} found it, and further on, a den under the roots. The den belongs to {X_indefinite}, which has taken to watching the paths.\n\n{B_nameDef}, who handles the colony's animals, wants to try taming it. Others want it dead before it decides people are food.

{A_nameDef} nearly stepped on {X_indefinite} sleeping in the brush near the colony. Its tracks go right past the storeroom, and twice now it has followed the haulers home, keeping a careful distance.\n\nThe council can send hunters, send {B_nameDef} out with a bucket of food, or hope it gets bored and wanders off.

li.label: Hunt it
li.outcome: The council marked {X_definite} for the hunters. {B_nameDef} called it a waste of a fine animal.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} try to tame it
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} has been put in charge of taming {X_definite}, and the others have been told to stay well back from the den.

li.label: Leave it alone
li.outcome: Left to its own business, {X_definite} has kept to its den so far. The haulers have started carrying sticks.
li.riskOutcome: The council left {X_definite} alone. It didn't return the favor: it came out of the brush at a dead run, straight for the nearest person.

texts.li: "It's very clean and it's very quiet and I'll do all the work and you won't even know it's there." {A_nameDef} said it to the council in one breath, and had clearly practiced. It is {X_indefinite}, and {A_nameDef} has been feeding it behind the storeroom for a week, out of {A_possessive} own dinner.\n\nIt has a name, which only {A_nameDef} is allowed to say. The adults suspect the feeding and cleaning will end up with the handlers.

There is {X_indefinite} following {A_nameDef} around the colony at a careful distance. {A_nameDef} swears it came on its own, though the trail of berries says otherwise.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to keep it. It's another mouth, it's wild, and it will chew something important. {A_nameDef} has heard all of that and is still standing there.

li.label: Let {A_objective} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has a pet now, and has introduced it to every person in the colony. It sleeps at the foot of {A_possessive} bed.

li.label: Let the handlers try, properly
li.outcome: The council put {X_definite} on the handlers' list. {A_nameDef} has been following the handlers around ever since, giving advice.

li.label: No, and that's final
li.outcome: No pet. {A_nameDef} has been sulking, loudly, in whichever room the council happens to be in.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} was told no, and set off past the fields toward wherever {X_definite} sleeps, without looking back.

texts.li: {X_nameDef}, the titled guest, ran a finger along the wall of the room {A_nameDef} built and studied the finger. "Charming," {X_nameDef} said. "And the rest of the year, I suppose, you keep pigs in it?" {A_nameDef} spent days on that room.\n\n{X_nameDef}'s patrons will hear how {X_nameDef} was treated here. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether the council will stand up for the work.

Over supper {X_nameDef} explained to the whole table that the servants' quarters back home are better built than the finest room in this colony, and looked straight at {A_nameDef} while saying it. {A_nameDef} raised most of the walls in the place.\n\nNo one at the table answered. Afterward {A_nameDef} came to the council to ask whether a title means you get to say that.

li.label: Say nothing and smile
li.outcome: No one contradicted {X_nameDef}, who took the silence as agreement and enjoyed the rest of the evening. {A_nameDef} spent the next day hammering at the workbench, harder than the work needed.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} answer back
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} told {X_nameDef} that out here a title won't keep the rain off, and that {A_nameDef}'s walls will. {X_nameDef} left the table, and {FACTION} will hear of it.

li.label: Ask what would please {X_objective}
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} asked {X_nameDef}, politely, what a proper room would look like. The answer took all afternoon. Since then {A_nameDef} has been frowning at the colony's rooms, one corner at a time.

texts.li: "Aching joints, bad dreams, low spirits, baldness." {X_nameDef}, the {FACTION} trader, has a small green bottle and a voice that carries. "One swallow, and the old feel thirty again." It's the last bottle, and it costs one hundred silver.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been suffering from most of those things lately, and can't stop looking at it.

{A_nameDef} hasn't slept properly in weeks, and {X_nameDef} the trader spotted it right away. Now there's a stoppered bottle on the table between them, and {X_nameDef} is explaining that it was brewed by hermits from a root that only grows on graves.\n\nIt costs one hundred silver. {A_nameDef} wants it, and the council holds the purse.

li.label: Buy {A_objective} the tonic
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} drank the tonic in one swallow, pulled a terrible face, and slept fourteen hours straight. {A_nameDef} woke up better than {A_pronoun} has been in weeks, and won't hear a word against the stuff.
li.riskOutcome: The tonic was water, sugar and something that tasted like an old boot. {A_nameDef} drank all of it anyway, out of spite, and people have been calling {A_objective} the alchemist since.

li.label: Make {X_nameDef} drink some first
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} took a swig, smacked {X_possessive} lips, and fell asleep on {X_possessive} own pack. When {X_nameDef} woke up, the council bought the rest for sixty silver.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} suddenly decided the tonic was far too precious for a trader to drink, packed it away in a huff, and wouldn't sell it after that.

li.label: Keep the silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} put the bottle away with a sigh. "Next time, maybe," {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, "if there's any left."

li.label: Have our doctor mix a sleeping draught
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} mixed {A_nameDef} a sleeping draught from the colony's own medicine. It tasted no better than the tonic would have, and {A_nameDef} slept until noon.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} boiled up a draught of herbs from the colony's own stores, bitter as bark. {A_nameDef} drank it, grimaced, and slept through to noon.
[b:past:healer] {B_nameDef} has treated a hundred bad sleepers and knew what to give. {A_nameDef} slept until noon, and {X_nameDef} put the tonic away with a sour look.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} knew {A_nameDef}'s face from across the yard. They met before, somewhere else, when {A_nameDef} was living a different life, and {X_nameDef} knows all about it ({SECRET}).\n\n"Keeping quiet is work," {X_nameDef} told {A_nameDef}, very friendly, "and work gets paid." One hundred and fifty silver ought to cover it.

{A_nameDef} went white when {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} walked in, and has been finding reasons to be elsewhere ever since. Tonight {A_nameDef} came to the council in private. {X_nameDef} knew {A_objective} before the colony, and knows something no one here does ({SECRET}).\n\n{X_nameDef} wants one hundred and fifty silver to keep it that way. {A_nameDef} can't pay that. The colony can.

li.label: Pay for {X_possessive} silence
li.outcome: The silver changed hands behind the storeroom. {X_nameDef} went back to the other visitors whistling, and {A_nameDef} finally got a decent night's sleep.
li.riskOutcome: The council paid {X_nameDef} a hundred and fifty silver to keep quiet. {X_nameDef} pocketed it and told the story anyway, while the coins were still warm.

li.label: Let {X_objective} talk
li.outcome: No silver, then. {X_nameDef} shrugged and told it to the first people {X_pronoun} could find, with details {A_nameDef} had managed to forget.

li.label: Threaten {X_objective}
li.outcome: A few of the colony's bigger people had a word with {X_nameDef} by the woodpile. {X_nameDef} has kept the secret since, and doesn't say much to anyone.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} explained to {X_nameDef} why talking would be unwise. {X_nameDef} answered by shouting the whole story across the yard, and a moment later the two of them were trading blows.

ColonyCouncil.DilemmaDef.label: the beast at the tree line

texts.li: It's back. {A_nameDef} saw {X_definite} at the tree line this morning, pacing the edge of the fields as if waiting for a door to be left open. It's the beast that mauled one of the colonists and limped off into the wild.

There are tracks around the colony again, deep ones, and {A_nameDef} knows whose they are. They belong to {X_definite}, the animal that tore into a colonist, got away, and earned itself a name.\n\nSome want it dead today. Some want it tamed, which doesn't sit well with the one it mauled.

li.label: Hunt it down now
li.outcome: A hunt, then. {A_nameDef} was the first to pick up a weapon.

li.label: Keep everyone inside
li.outcome: People are keeping close to the buildings until {X_definite} wanders off. The work is piling up, and tempers are getting short.

li.label: Try to tame it
li.outcome: The council marked {X_definite} for taming. If the handlers manage it, the colony will own the fiercest animal for miles. The handlers have gone very quiet since they heard.
li.riskOutcome: The first handler got halfway across the clearing before {X_definite} charged. Now it's loose among the buildings, hunting people.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} is the one who hurt {A_nameDef} and got away. Now {X_nameDef} sits in a cell, eating the colony's food and sleeping under the colony's roof, and {A_nameDef} has stood outside that door every night since the capture, saying nothing.\n\nThe council has to decide what {X_nameDef} is now: a debt to be settled, a mouth to be fed, or a pair of hands to be won over.

{A_nameDef} still carries what {X_nameDef} did, in the body and elsewhere. {X_nameDef} still has the nerve to ask the wardens for an extra blanket.\n\nThe colony wants to know what the council means to do with this prisoner. {A_nameDef} wants to know whether {A_possessive} say counts for anything.

li.label: Execute {X_objective}
li.outcome: The wardens have their orders. {A_nameDef} asked to be there when it happens, and the council agreed.

li.label: Let {X_objective} rot in there
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} stays in the cell, fed and ignored. {A_nameDef} no longer goes near that end of the colony.

li.label: Try to recruit {X_objective}
li.outcome: The wardens have begun working on {X_nameDef}. When {A_nameDef} heard, {A_pronoun} put down {A_possessive} spoon and left the table, and a few of {A_possessive} friends went with {A_objective}.

texts.li: One hundred and twenty silver, on the spot. {X_nameDef} of {FACTION} has fallen hard for {PET_nameDef}, {A_nameDef}'s animal, and it's a very good price.\n\n{A_nameDef} has been standing between {X_nameDef} and {PET_nameDef} ever since the offer was made.

Every time the {FACTION} visitors pass {PET_nameDef}, {X_nameDef} stops to scratch an ear and mutters about money. Today {X_nameDef} made a real offer: one hundred and twenty silver, right now, and {PET_nameDef} goes home with {X_nameDef}.\n\nThe colony could use the silver. Some say {PET_nameDef} would be safer somewhere that gets raided less. {A_nameDef} hasn't said a word, and has started brushing {PET_nameDef} very thoroughly.

li.label: Sell {PET_objective}
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} counted the silver into {A_nameDef}'s hand and took {PET_definite} by the lead. {PET_nameDef} went along without a fuss. {A_nameDef} kept the silver shut in {A_possessive} fist for a long while afterward.

li.label: Name a price {X_nameDef} won't pay
li.outcome: The council asked two hundred and fifty silver, expecting a no. {X_nameDef} paid on the spot without haggling, and the animal went home with {X_objective}.
li.riskOutcome: "Robbery," said {X_nameDef}, at two hundred and fifty silver, and went back to {X_possessive} people empty-handed, as the council had hoped.

li.label: Not for sale
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} gave {PET_definite} one last scratch behind the ears and went back to {X_possessive} people. {A_nameDef} is keeping {PET_nameDef} on a short lead until {X_nameDef} is well down the road.

texts.li: {X_nameDef} travels with the {FACTION} party and carries a bag of dried roots and bone needles. {X_nameDef} took one look at the way {A_nameDef} moves and offered to see to the old injury, for eighty silver.\n\n{B_nameDef}, who does most of the colony's doctoring, wants to watch and learn, though {B_pronoun} suspects half of what's in that bag is dirt.

{A_nameDef} has favored an old injury for as long as anyone can remember. When it came out that {X_nameDef}, one of the {FACTION} visitors, is a healer, {A_nameDef} went to ask and came back with a price. For eighty silver, {X_nameDef} will see what can be done.\n\n{B_nameDef} has offered to assist, mostly to keep an eye on what goes into {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Pay the healer
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} worked on {A_nameDef} with hot stones and strong hands for most of the afternoon while {B_nameDef} watched every move. The old injury still aches, but less.
li.riskOutcome: {X_nameDef} rubbed something brown into {A_nameDef}'s old injury, hummed over it a while, and was gone with the silver before supper. {B_nameDef} learned a few things not to do.

li.label: Pay {X_objective} to teach {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: For sixty silver {X_nameDef} spent the afternoon teaching {B_nameDef} what everything in the bag is for, using {A_nameDef}'s old injury for practice. {A_nameDef} was poked a great deal and helped not at all.

li.label: Keep the silver
li.outcome: {X_nameDef} went back to the {FACTION} camp with the bag still tied shut, and {A_nameDef} went on favoring the old injury, making sure the council saw it.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} treat it, with our own medicine
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} worked on {A_nameDef}'s old injury all afternoon with the colony's own medicine, while {X_nameDef} watched and offered advice {B_nameDef} hadn't asked for. It aches less now.

outcomes.li: [lowtech] {B_nameDef} made a poultice from the colony's herbs and bound {A_nameDef}'s old injury in clean linen. {X_nameDef} looked at the work and said it would do.
[b:trait:Kind] {B_nameDef} took {B_possessive} time over {A_nameDef}'s old injury and explained every step. It aches less, and {A_nameDef} says it was the explaining that helped.
